question.text: In a Value Averaging Investment Plan, compared to a regular SIP, the investor:

answer.text: Invests the same fixed amount every period regardless of market conditions
Invests more when the market is down and less when the market is up
Stops investing when the market is at all-time highs

explanation.text: The Logic: In a Value Averaging Investment Plan, the contribution is adjusted to keep the portfolio on a target growth path. When prices are down, more is invested to make up the shortfall; when prices are up, less is invested. This contrasts with a fixed SIP amount that does not vary with market levels. The Trap: A regular SIP invests a fixed amount each period regardless of market direction; value averaging varies the amount based on whether the portfolio is below or above its target value. Note: The defining feature is the variable instalment driven by the gap between actual and target portfolio value.
